segments.text: Launching and scaling a tech venture
requires significant time, effort, and money.
It's also risky, which is why aligning your offering
with market demand and customer needs
is crucial to your success.
An effective way to do that is by finding product market
fit, using a four step process based on entrepreneur Eric
Ries's lean startup approach.
The first step is ideation.
Building a satisfactory product begins
with understanding and devising solutions
to your target customer's problem.
Think about addressing their pain points in a way that's not
just innovative, but viable.
Next, translate your vision into hypotheses
that cover each part of your business model,
including your customer value proposition,
go to market plan and profit formula.
Your hypotheses should be falsifiable,
meaning you can prove whether they're true or false.
After forming your hypothesis, test them.
The most efficient way is with a rough version of your offering,
better known as your minimum viable product or MVP.
Your MVP should include features that
don't take substantial time to develop, and be usable enough
to assess your hypothesis and provide insights
for future experiments.
Lastly, decide which tests to run and their sequence.
Consider your strategy, resources, time and team,
and prioritize those that can best
uncover your ideas potential.
After completing all four steps, execute your tests and measure
their results to determine whether to modify
your hypothesis, shut down your company or scale,
because you've achieved product market fit.
Although it can be challenging, finding your product market fit
is critical to getting your tech venture off the ground.
By understanding your customers and generating and testing
viable solutions to their needs, you
can set yourself on the path to entrepreneurial success.
To learn more about product market fit
and navigating the startup ecosystem,
